scope: 48 Biology catalog labs plus Sordaria extension. All suggestions are delivery planning, separate from user approval and physical classroom validation.

existing-classroom.label: Virtual + classroom guidance exists
existing-classroom.readiness: Classroom data/model route and guidance already exist; local teacher pilot and user acceptance are separate.

physical-candidate.label: Virtual now; classroom practical proposed
physical-candidate.readiness: Classroom adaptation needs its own procedure, materials, student/teacher PDFs, measurement plan and teacher pilot. App classroom entry is not implemented.

model-candidate.label: Virtual now; classroom model/data activity proposed
model-candidate.readiness: A paper, token, tool or supplied-data activity can teach the concepts; a classroom version and matching resources still need development and review. This does not reproduce the actual biological process.

keep-virtual.label: Keep virtual by design
keep-virtual.readiness: Retain the requested virtual-only lab. A paper reinforcement activity would be a separate optional supplement, not an implemented classroom mode.

blind.title: Exploratorium: Blind Spot
blind.basis: Comparable printed-card perception and approximate geometry activity.

lung.title: Australian National University: How to make a lung model

transp.title: Science & Plants for Schools: investigating transpiration with a potometer
transp.basis: Comparable water-uptake and mass-loss measurements; these are distinct measurements.

bird.title: HHMI BioInteractive: Beaks As Tools
bird.basis: Comparable hands-on feeding-tool model for environment-dependent selective advantage.

key.title: National Park Service: Using Dichotomous Keys
key.basis: Comparable student-built and peer-tested keys using visible traits in pictures.

seeds.title: University of Florida / partner universities: Seed Germination
seeds.basis: Scientific basis for water uptake and root emergence; not a classroom protocol.

amylase.title: University of Maryland: Starch Hydrolysis by Amylase
amylase.basis: Scientific/experimental precedent only. This university protocol is not adopted as a ninth-grade classroom procedure.

drift.title: National Human Genome Research Institute: Genetic Drift
drift.basis: Scientific basis for random allele-frequency changes; bead adaptation is a planning proposal.

population.title: OpenStax Biology 2e: Population Demography
population.basis: Scientific basis for quadrats and mark-recapture; bean/population model is a planning proposal.

corridors.title: University of Wisconsin Damschen Research Lab: Habitat corridors
corridors.basis: Scientific basis for connectivity questions; printed fictional map remains a teaching model.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare germination in seeds given different water conditions; record germination and root growth.
labs.learningEvidence: Use observations to separate water availability from other growing conditions.
labs.workNeeded: Define species, germination criterion, timing, independent samples and matched growing conditions.

labs.classroomActivity: Count retained drops on a coin and compare water with a teacher-prepared detergent mixture.
labs.learningEvidence: Use measured comparisons to explain cohesion and surface behavior.
labs.workNeeded: Calibrate the actual dropper; do not assume the virtual drop volume or counts.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare food samples and known controls with school-approved indicator tests.
labs.learningEvidence: Use positive/negative controls to support limited claims about food molecules.
labs.workNeeded: Author reagent, heating, disposal and observation procedures; use genuine observations rather than expected colors.

labs.classroomActivity: Observe calibrated plant/animal slides and record actual measurements.
labs.learningEvidence: Use calibrated scales to compare visible cells and state sampling limits.
labs.workNeeded: Existing materials/procedure and classroom entry; teacher verifies slides, calibration and class setup.

labs.classroomActivity: Use a teacher-reviewed dialysis-tubing mass-change investigation alongside the existing accepted lab conditions.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain water movement using measured mass change and concentration relationships.
labs.workNeeded: Retain the accepted virtual lab and A/D condition wording; classroom preparation/data collection require their own confirmation and worksheet.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare potato catalase reactions using the documented gas-collection procedure.
labs.learningEvidence: Use early gas-volume rates and controls to reason about enzyme activity.
labs.workNeeded: Existing starting quantities and apparatus still require the documented local teacher pilot.

labs.classroomActivity: Collect gas from matched yeast/sugar comparisons using the existing classroom apparatus options.
labs.learningEvidence: Compare actual gas changes and retain measurement/replicate provenance.
labs.workNeeded: Use the matching balloon, cylinder or syringe handout and validated class preparation.

labs.classroomActivity: Use matched leaf-disk preparations and record floating disks under different light conditions.
labs.learningEvidence: Interpret flotation evidence, controls and sample differences.
labs.workNeeded: Use existing classroom guidance; physical preparation and observation times need a local pilot.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare growth in matched plants using the documented signal/carrier comparison.
labs.learningEvidence: Use change from starting height and independent plants to reason about a signal effect.
labs.workNeeded: Teacher selects an educational preparation and approved supplier instructions; growing takes multiple days.

labs.classroomActivity: Count stages in non-overlapping fields on prepared root-tip slides.
labs.learningEvidence: Compare stage proportions and distinguish observations from an assumed cycle length.
labs.workNeeded: Existing classroom counts and guide; verify slide quality and classification criteria.

labs.classroomActivity: Use the existing paper chromosome-strip model for crossing over and cell division.
labs.learningEvidence: Track allele combinations while distinguishing homologs, sister chromatids and the modeled pathways.
labs.workNeeded: Classroom counterpart is a chromosome model rather than a live-cell experiment.

labs.classroomActivity: Count traits on corn ears from documented crosses and compare ears and pooled results.
labs.learningEvidence: Compare observed ratios with predictions while retaining meaningful sampling.
labs.workNeeded: Use the documented cross/traits; preserve the user-reviewed corn lab.

labs.classroomActivity: Score supplied fly-cross images/data, or use an approved documented educational cross.
labs.learningEvidence: Estimate recombination from parental/recombinant classes and sample size.
labs.workNeeded: Existing guidance includes an image/data alternative; live crosses need lead time and the supplier protocol.

labs.classroomActivity: Extract crude material from fruit using the existing complete preparation and controls.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain membranes, separation, precipitation and the limits of visible material.
labs.workNeeded: Teacher confirms the existing extraction guidance against the local school procedure, including its controls.

labs.classroomActivity: Use a suitable educational cell-free expression kit and its supported controls.
labs.learningEvidence: Use reporter evidence to connect DNA information with protein production.
labs.workNeeded: Kit-dependent: follow the supplier protocol and use only comparisons the kit actually supports.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare growth and fluorescence with the documented educational arabinose-controlled reporter system.
labs.learningEvidence: Distinguish carrying a reporter from expressing it and distinguish selection from induction.
labs.workNeeded: This stable legacy ID does not mean the current lab is a literal lac-operon experiment; use its actual reporter kit and approved classroom protocol.

labs.classroomActivity: Separate prepared DNA fragments with a ladder and measure migration.
labs.learningEvidence: Use a calibration relationship to compare and estimate fragment sizes.
labs.workNeeded: Existing classroom procedure; use approved equipment, stain and supplier settings.

labs.classroomActivity: Use different tools as beaks to collect different seed types, then model survival, inheritance and a new generation.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain why food conditions change the advantage of inherited beak differences.
labs.workNeeded: A feeding contest alone does not show evolution: retain an explicit inheritance/reproduction step and separate tool performance from real bird data.

labs.classroomActivity: Draw colored beads from matched allele pools and compare changes in small and large populations.
labs.learningEvidence: Distinguish random sampling from selection and compare variation among independent model populations.
labs.workNeeded: Define what each bead represents; use fresh independent draws when testing variability.

labs.classroomActivity: Build and compare trees using printed character tables and labeled synthetic DNA-sequence cards.
labs.learningEvidence: Justify shared ancestry from evidence rather than arranging similar-looking pictures.
labs.workNeeded: Supply comparable character evidence, alternative trees and a reviewed scoring/explanation key.

labs.classroomActivity: Use a contact-network board, tokens and event cards to model transmission and prevention.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain how network contacts and interventions affect spread.
labs.workNeeded: Keep the contacts and model rules explicit; use fictional case information rather than personal health records.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare prepared cell images and supplied metabolic-test cards for the fictional profiles.
labs.learningEvidence: Use several lines of evidence to distinguish profiles and explain what remains uncertain.
labs.workNeeded: Prepare consistent reference evidence; retain this as a supplied-data activity rather than culturing unknown organisms.

labs.classroomActivity: Observe movement in school-approved educational protist samples; use prepared images or slides for structure and videos when motion cannot be observed.
labs.learningEvidence: Connect visible locomotion structures with movement and distinguish observations from identification claims.
labs.workNeeded: Choose specimens and handling procedures; prepared fixed slides cannot demonstrate live movement.

labs.classroomActivity: Examine a store-bought mushroom and prepared fungal slides or labeled microscopy images.
labs.learningEvidence: Connect visible fungal structures with growth and reproduction.
labs.workNeeded: Specify the specimen/reference images and observable features; this is not wild-mushroom identification or a mold-culture project.

labs.classroomActivity: Inspect moss and fern specimens, then use prepared images and stage cards to connect life-cycle stages.
labs.learningEvidence: Distinguish gametophyte/sporophyte stages and the roles of spores and gametes.
labs.workNeeded: Provide the stages not visible on the available specimens; do not claim to observe an entire life cycle during one class.

labs.classroomActivity: Build paper seed models and compare measured descent or dispersal under matched conditions.
labs.learningEvidence: Use evidence to explain how shape affects the model seed movement.
labs.workNeeded: Define mass, release height, airflow, measurement method and meaningful repeats; physical models are not real plant fitness measurements.

labs.classroomActivity: Classify prepared specimens, models or complete organism images using visible body-plan traits.
labs.learningEvidence: Justify classifications with observable features, including exceptions and limits.
labs.workNeeded: Choose reference material where the necessary traits can actually be seen; an image activity can replace specimens.

labs.classroomActivity: Use specimen/photo cards to build a dichotomous key, then have another group test it with new examples.
labs.learningEvidence: Show that each paired choice uses a visible, useful distinction.
labs.workNeeded: Prepare suitable examples and a test set; complete a teacher review of key wording and ambiguities.

labs.classroomActivity: Measure corresponding bones in replicas or scaled images and compare limb structures.
labs.learningEvidence: Use homologous parts as evidence while distinguishing ancestry from present function.
labs.workNeeded: Supply reliable scale bars and measurement rules; compare the same anatomical structures.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare plant water loss or water uptake using teacher-prepared weighing/potometer setups.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain the effect of an environmental condition and distinguish uptake from measured mass loss.
labs.workNeeded: Select one validated apparatus and define controls, units and preparation; do not treat uptake as a direct equivalent of every transpiration measurement.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare drainage and retained water in measured soil columns.
labs.learningEvidence: Use a water balance to distinguish drainage, retention and claims about plant-available water.
labs.workNeeded: Define soil preparation, sample size, water input, drainage time and evaporation controls.

labs.classroomActivity: Observe real flower parts and model pollen transfer; use stage cards for fertilization and seed formation.
labs.learningEvidence: Distinguish pollination from fertilization and connect structures with their roles.
labs.workNeeded: Choose suitable specimens and observation tools; visible pollen transfer does not demonstrate fertilization.

labs.classroomActivity: Measure cooling in different-sized containers of the same shape/material and calculate surface-area-to-volume ratios.
labs.learningEvidence: Distinguish total surface area from area per volume and interpret model cooling evidence.
labs.workNeeded: Author starting conditions, sensor placement and measurement rules; this is a physical heat-transfer model, not animal thermoregulation.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare starch breakdown with educational amylase, matched controls and an approved starch indicator.
labs.learningEvidence: Use controls and observations to explain enzyme action and the limits of a starch test.
labs.workNeeded: Develop a school-level reagent/temperature/timing protocol; use supplied enzyme rather than student saliva.

labs.classroomActivity: Measure ruler-drop responses and compare repeated observations under a controlled condition.
labs.learningEvidence: Interpret real variation and explain the limits of the distance-to-time model.
labs.workNeeded: Define the release cue, anticipation controls and justified repeat count; keep individual results private if recorded by name.

labs.classroomActivity: Use printed dot/cross targets and measured viewing distances to compare disappearance and reappearance.
labs.learningEvidence: Connect an observation with the optic-disc model and explain approximate geometry.
labs.workNeeded: Create print-scale and viewing instructions plus an alternative supplied-data route; this is not a clinical vision test.

labs.classroomActivity: Move glucose, signal and liver-store tokens through meal/fasting scenarios.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain negative feedback and the distinct roles of insulin and glucagon.
labs.workNeeded: Keep model units, storage and response rules explicit; the activity does not measure or change real blood glucose.

labs.classroomActivity: Use a hinged arm model, a small load and a force meter to compare attachment points.
labs.learningEvidence: Use measurements to relate lever arms, force and turning effects.
labs.workNeeded: Define apparatus geometry, fixed loads and measurement limits; classroom arm models are not measurements of a student muscle.

labs.classroomActivity: Use a teacher-prepared bottle/balloon diaphragm model to observe changes in balloon volume.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain the relationship between pressure, volume and air movement.
labs.workNeeded: Author construction and observation instructions and discuss the rigid bottle and balloon model limits.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare water flow through tubes of different internal radius at a controlled driving pressure.
labs.learningEvidence: Use outflow measurements to explain how tube geometry affects resistance.
labs.workNeeded: Specify head/pressure, tube length, radius, fluid and timing; this is a hydraulic analogy rather than actual blood flow.

labs.classroomActivity: Move labeled substance tokens on a printed nephron board through filtration, reabsorption and secretion.
labs.learningEvidence: Distinguish the three processes and account for where each substance ends up.
labs.workNeeded: Provide reviewed transport rules; a simple sieve alone cannot represent selective reabsorption or secretion.

labs.classroomActivity: Use matching antigen/receptor cards and memory-cell tokens for first and later encounters.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain why later responses can differ and what the memory-cell model represents.
labs.workNeeded: Define the time/response model and limits; this is a model, not an exposure or immunity test.

labs.classroomActivity: Use clay or paper cell models to order cleavage, blastula and gastrulation stages.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain changes in cell arrangement and distinguish them from simple growth.
labs.workNeeded: Choose a consistent organism context and reviewed stage diagrams; stage models do not reproduce live development.

labs.classroomActivity: Compare nearby schoolyard microhabitats with light, temperature/moisture readings and visible organism observations.
labs.learningEvidence: Use measurements and sampling to support a limited habitat comparison.
labs.workNeeded: Define field boundaries, instrument methods and comparable sampling; student observations need not match virtual values.

labs.classroomActivity: Use mixed beans or beads for a mark-recapture model; a separate plant/quadrat extension can use field observations.
labs.learningEvidence: Explain sampling assumptions and compare an estimate with a known model population.
labs.workNeeded: Specify mixing, marking, equal capture chance and a closed population; quadrats are a different sampling method.

labs.classroomActivity: Move counted energy tokens through food-web cards and record transfers and losses.
labs.learningEvidence: Track an energy budget and distinguish energy flow from matter cycling.
labs.workNeeded: State the chosen transfer rules; do not turn an illustrative efficiency into a universal ten-percent law.

labs.classroomActivity: Print the fictional landscape and choose protected cells using the same budget and habitat/connectivity constraints.
labs.learningEvidence: Use the map and budget to justify tradeoffs and evaluate model predictions.
labs.workNeeded: Prepare scale-correct map/cards and scoring rules; predicted persistence is not a measured conservation outcome.

labs.classroomActivity: Keep the interactive enzyme-placement lab virtual; a paper DNA/RNA/codon model could be an optional separate reinforcement activity.
labs.learningEvidence: Connect enzyme action, base pairing and process location without changing the reviewed lab.
labs.workNeeded: The user explicitly requested a virtual-only lab. A physical supplement is not a change to its current delivery mode.

labs.classroomActivity: Count ordered asci on prepared Sordaria cross slides, retaining fields and uncertain observations.
labs.learningEvidence: Use segregation patterns and sampling limits to estimate gene-to-centromere distance.
labs.workNeeded: Prepared slides are the basic classroom route; culturing is not required.
